summary: Hermann Wilhelm Ebel was a linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1836-1839) and at the University of Halle-Wittenberg under August Friedrich Pott (~1839-1842). He held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1872 to 1875.

Hermann von Schlagintweit worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1844-1848) and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1851 to 1854.
Hideaki Kimura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (~1978-1984), where he also served as a researcher.

Hideaki Nakatani works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao (1966), was a disciple of Yutaka Ochihara, and earned a PhD from Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1982). He served as professor at Kobe Gakuin University (~1990-2017).
Hidehiko Kurita is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He earned a PhD from Tohoku University (~2008-2013) and served as a lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University around 2018.
Hideki Kiyoshima is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi and held an appointment as a lecturer at Kindai University.
Hidenaka Tanaka was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1906-1909) and held a position at Kyoto Women's University from around 1949 to 1958.
Hidenori Kitagawa was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Hakuju Ui. He served as a professor at Nagoya University from around 1956 to 1969.

Hidenori S. Sakuma works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied under Seiichi Kato at the University of Tokyo (~1974-1983) and Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg (~1983-1990). Posts included Shitennoji University (1991), University of Tsukuba (~1996-2003), and Taisho University.

Hideo Mineshima was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University (~1948-1953). He served as a professor at Waseda University (~1974-1998) and held posts at Bunkyo Gakuin University (~1998-2003) and Sanko Research Institute.
Hideo Sakurai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1940-1943). He held a post as professor emeritus at Komazawa University from around 1965 to 1990.

Hideomi Yaita is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University (~1978-1983). He held posts as a research assistant at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1985) and as a lecturer at Taisho University.
Hideto Ono is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University (~1963-1967). He served as an associate professor at Aichi Gakuin University from around 1983 to 1989.

Hideyo Ogawa is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Hiroshima University (~1973-1982). He served as a professor of Indian philosophy in the Graduate School of Letters at Hiroshima University from around 1988 to 2020.
Hideyuki Matsumori is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies and held a post as an assistant professor at Soka University.
Hildegard Diemberger is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. Her work was supervised by Anne-Marie Blondeau, Luciano Petech, and Ernst Steinkellner from around 1990 to 1996.

Himanshu Prabha Ray is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Panjab University, the University of Cambridge, and Jawaharlal Nehru University. Her posts include Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1986-2006), the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies (2005), and LMU Munich.

Hiram W. Woodward is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Harvard College (~1958-1962) and Yale University (~1967-1975). He held posts at the University of Michigan (~1972-1982), University of Vermont (~1982-1986), and Walters Art Museum (~1986-2011).

Hirananda Sastri was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at DAV College Lahore, Oriental College, and Panjab University. His posts included DAV College (~1900-1903), the Archaeological Survey of India (1903-1906), Nagpur and Lucknow museums (1906-1917), and Baroda State Archaeology (1934-1942).
Hiroaki Yokoyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University, where he also held a post as a research student.
